newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK June Purchasing Managers Index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK June Purchasing Managers Index.

text.p: Following are a selection of analysts comments on Britain's June purchasing managers index which fell to 53.4 from 54.4 in May -- showing the 13th successive monthly expansion in manufacturing.

"Price pressures remain well under control. The price index still remains well below 50, the strength of sterling is keeping input prices well under control. The strength of the pound is not having a major effect on exports yet. But perhaps there are the first signs of that coming through."

"The survey is weaker than we expected with growth in manufacturing continuing at a slightly slower pace. To that extent it corroborates the CBI survey which suggests output is struggling to pick up. The PMI suggests the pound's strength is hitting exports. But it is encouraging that export growth has not been hit too much because of economic growth in our trading partners."

"The numbers look a bit weaker but we're still above the magic 50 level. The component indices are all looking a little bit softer. Manufacturing is growing but not at a particularly strong pace. It's a further indication that manufacturers are being squeezed by the pound and only supported by the strength of consumer demand.

It suggests the export sector remains subdued. The question is whether Gordon Brown can achieve any respite for the export sector with his budget and the answer is probably not. He would have to tighten fiscal policy by more than is politically feasible to have a significant impact."

"On the face of it these numbers are a touch softer than expected and we might see the pound down a bit but overall they do reflect a fairly robust economy. We will see a fairly tight budget but I don't think it will preclude the need for further rises in interest rates."
